fragen.frage: What unique shape is wombat poo?
Which future Australian prime minister set a world record for speed beer drinking in 1954 (1.4 litres in 11 seconds)?
What was Melbourne briefly called when it was founded in 1835?
In 1932 the Australian army officially declared “war” on an animal species – and lost. Which one?
In 1967 the serving prime minister Harold Holt vanished without a trace while swimming. What was named after him?
antworten: A swimming pool (Harold Holt Memorial Swimming Centre)

fragen.frage: Australia has a gigantic coastline. Roughly how many beaches are there on the continent?
Which country exports camels to Saudi Arabia because it has the world's largest wild camel population?
The platypus is one of the few venomous mammals. Where is the male's venom?
antworten: In the spurs on its hind legs
At the base of its tail
In the claws of its front feet

fragen.frage: How long is Australia's famous Dingo Fence, the longest fence in the world?
Believe it or not: in winter the Australian Alps get snow over a larger area on average than which European country?
Which ground-breaking aviation safety invention was developed by the Australian David Warren in 1953?
Roughly how many kangaroos live in Australia (compared with about 26 million people)?
Fraser Island (K'gari) is the world's largest... what?
Based on toxicity tests, which snake is considered the most venomous land animal in the world?
How long is Highway 1, which runs all the way around the Australian mainland (the longest national highway in the world)?
What was the historic peak ratio of sheep to people in Australia in the 20th century?
Why did an Australian brewer invent the spread “Vegemite” in 1922?
antworten: As military rations for the jungle
Because of a shortage of peanut butter

fragen.frage: Uluru (Ayers Rock) is a monolith. Roughly what percentage of the rock is thought to lie below the surface?
In which state was it once illegal to wear pink hot pants after midday on a Sunday?
The Irukandji jellyfish is extremely venomous and causes the dreaded Irukandji syndrome. How big is its bell?
Which wireless networking technology we use every day is largely based on patents of the Australian science agency CSIRO?
Why is the famous Lake Hillier on Middle Island permanently bright pink?
antworten: Because of algae (Dunaliella salina) and extreme salinity
Because of light refracted by corals

fragen.frage: Australia has compulsory voting for citizens. Roughly how much is the fine for not voting in a federal election for the first time without an excuse?
Australia's largest cattle station (Anna Creek Station) is bigger than which European country?
How many cane toads were originally released in 1935 to fight beetles in the sugar cane (today there are hundreds of millions)?
The Great Barrier Reef is so huge it can be seen from space. Roughly how many individual reefs is it made of?
Some places in Australia (such as Eucla or Lord Howe Island) have a very unusual time zone. What makes it special?
antworten: They change the time every 3 months
They are offset from UTC by 30 or 45 minutes
They don't use daylight saving, but turn their clocks back

fragen.frage: Because of the anatomy of their hind legs and tail, what can kangaroos hardly do at all?
For years, what share of the world's poker machines (“pokies”) did Australia have relative to its small population?
antworten: About 20 % (excluding casino meccas like Las Vegas)

fragen.frage: What percentage of the Australian continent counts as desert or arid/semi-arid land?
Who became the first official postmaster of New South Wales in 1810 – and was actually a convict?
In which marsupial does the pouch open BACKWARDS (downwards), so no dirt gets in while digging?
Which pretty sea snail in Queensland waters can kill people with its venomous harpoons?
The train “The Ghan” crosses Australia from north to south. Where does its name come from?
antworten: From the Afghan cameleers of the 19th century

fragen.frage: On which famous Australian highway (Stuart Highway) were there long stretches in the Northern Territory without a speed limit for a long time?
How big is a baby kangaroo (joey) right after birth?
antworten: The size of a jelly bean / strawberry (about 2 cm)

fragen.frage: Eucalypts make up most of Australia's forests. How many different eucalyptus species are there in Australia?
In 1869 the largest gold nugget ever found was discovered in Victoria. What was it called?
Which bird is known for a call that sounds like a person laughing out loud?
On which famous island is it strictly forbidden to feed or approach the purebred wild dingoes living there?
Quokkas are famous for their permanent smile. On which Western Australian island do they mainly live?
What does the Australian road sign “Road Trains Give Way” mean?
antworten: CAREFUL: you have to give way/make room for the huge trucks up to 53 m long!
The road is closed to road trains

fragen.frage: Which Australian city is geographically considered the most isolated city of over a million people in the world?
How many ceramic tiles make up the roof of the famous Sydney Opera House?
Which flightless bird of the Queensland rainforest is considered the most dangerous bird in the world because of its razor-sharp dagger claws?
Which beer is known around the world as “the Australian beer”, but is hardly drunk by Aussies themselves?
How many convicts were transported from Great Britain to Australia between 1788 and 1868?
Since when, thanks to antivenom, has there been not a single documented death from a funnel-web spider bite in Australia, despite hundreds of bites?
On which Australian external territory island do millions of red land crabs migrate from the forest to the sea every year?
Which organisation once used pedal-powered generators for radios to provide medical care in the vast outback?

levels.text: You probably thought Sydney was the capital and kangaroos give kids a lift to school. In the outback you wouldn't last 20 minutes before a huntsman finished you off with a dirty look. Grab a cold one and start again, mate!

You've seen Vegemite on toast before (and probably spat it out again). You know where Down Under is, but on the hard facts you still mix up bunyips with cute wombats. Better not head into the bush without a guide just yet!
Respect! You know your stuff. You know not to hug a cassowary and that Bob Hawke was a legend. You'd survive a week in the Red Centre without having to eat your own shoes. Solid, mate!

Crikey! You're almost a local. You speak fluent Aussie slang, know the dark corners of the history and flick venomous spiders away without blinking. Even the crocs in the Northern Territory give you a respectful nod.

Fair dinkum, mate! Nobody can fool you – you practically helped build the place! You have snake venom for breakfast, personally fought the emus in 1932 and know exactly how to reverse-park a kangaroo. You're not just an expert, you ARE Australia!
